title: Enrollment Records and Entry Types under Student Enrollment, Transfers and Pre-Kindergarten Admissions
content:
**Rule.** Under Student Enrollment, Transfers and Pre-Kindergarten Admissions, a household may enroll any number of students; there is no limit per household. Each enrollment record covers one student for one school year. A student is registered only when the student has no other enrollment for the same school year in status provisional or enrolled, so a student holds at most 1 open enrollment (provisional or enrolled) in any school year.

**Entry types.** A student who withdrew may be registered again in the same school year with the entry type re-entry. A continuing student is registered for each new school year with the entry type returning student. A student who has never attended the district before is new to the district.

## Judging a new registration

The check is made on the district's enrollment records, matched on the same student and the same school year, before the registration is made.

| The same student already holds, for the same school year | Registration |
|---|---|
| an enrollment in status provisional | not made |
| an enrollment in status enrolled | not made |
| only an enrollment in status withdrawn | may be made, with entry type re-entry |
| no enrollment | may be made |

An enrollment of the same student for a different school year does not count, whatever its status.

## Examples (hypothetical)

- A household registers three children for the same school year. Each child gets an own enrollment record, and nothing limits the number of children.
- A student withdrew in October and the family returns in January of the same school year. The October record is withdrawn, not provisional or enrolled, so the student may be registered again, with entry type re-entry.
- A student completed the previous school year and is registered for the next one. The earlier record belongs to a different school year, so the new registration is made, with entry type returning student.
